newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds firm, placing final bets.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds firm, placing final bets.

text.p: *Australian bond prices closed firm as the market made its final preparations for Wednesday's expected easing in official interest rates after Tuesday's RBA board meeting.
*Victorian state capital closed Tuesday for Melbourne Cup.
Australian bond prices closed firm on Monday as the market made its final preparations for Wednesday's expected easing in official interest rates after Tuesday's Reserve Bank board meeting.
The recent run of data, including today's ANZ October job advertisement series, are seen pointing to a sluggish economy in need of a further stimulus from a monetary policy easing.

But some traders feel the market is running the risk of 'buying the rumour, selling the fact' with a 1/2 point easing having been priced in for some time, unless the RBA appears not to rule out the possibility of a further cut down the track.
Indeed, the March 1997 bill futures contract is already pricing in a 75 basis point easing in current 7.0 percent official interest rates by the end of the first quarter.

Traders said that today's trading action was fairly light with odd-lot buying having exaggerated price movements, and Tuesday is unlikely to be any better with the Victorian state capital closed for the Melbourne Cup.
However, most of Australia is likely to briefly close down while the horse race is on tomorrow afternoon.
Meanwhile, the only certainty for the market would appear seem to be the outcome of Tuesday's U.S. Presidential election.

The incumbent President, Bill Clinton, is widely to tipped to retain office, although a Democratic win to take control of the House of Representative could cause a stir in the U.S. Treasury market as they are seen as bigger spenders, which could boost the budget deficit.
"And among all this we have the quarterly refunding auctions, which could put pressure on yields both in the U.S. and here," one trader added.
The Treasury will be offering US$38.5 billion of securities over three days starting Tuesday.

The local market ended a six day run of underperformance against the U.S. after U.S. Treasuries took profits on Friday, while bonds here firmed on rate cut hopes. However, the market continued to drag its heels against Canada, which is also starting to price in a further easing by the Bank of Canada.
